BAX.thesis_one_line: Hospital supplies maker with recovering sales, but heavy debt and a guidance raise that is mostly a one-time tariff refund.
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raise of $0.10 at the midpoint is about equal to a $0.11 one-off IEEPA tariff refund in Q2 (8-K 0001628280-26-050795).

Net debt about $7.3B (Baxter consolidated, 30 Jun 2026), roughly 3.9x TTM adjusted EBITDA (my estimate); net leverage covenant maximum raised for five quarters on 18 Aug 2026 (8-K 0001628280-26-057739); S&P and Moody's outlooks Negative.
FY2025 adjusted EPS of $2.27 missed the twice-cut guide of $2.35-$2.40; Q4 2025 adjusted EPS $0.44 vs guided $0.52-$0.57; GAAP continuing EPS -$1.75 in FY2025.
Novum IQ pump shipment and installation hold since July 2025 with release timing uncertain; securities class action (filed Oct 2025) and DOJ CID/subpoena on Hillrom.
CFO turnover: interim CFO resigned effective 15 Sep 2026; new CFO starts 1 Oct 2026.
data_conflicts: b1/Q07 triage cited net debt/EBITDA about 4.0x; filing-based estimate is 3.9x (consistent) but the covenant definition is not in the text I read.
Adjusted EPS excludes about $0.6B a year of intangible amortisation while GAAP continuing EPS was -$1.75 in FY2025; d4 NTM P/E of 11.5x is on an adjusted basis.
TTM FCF of $839M is flattered by working-capital release; FY2025 FCF was $438M.
BAX.next_earnings_date_basis: estimate from prior-year pattern (30 Oct 2025); not announced in filings opened
BAX.confidence_in_thesis: low: turnaround evidence is one good quarter helped by a one-off, and covenant headroom was loosened by amendment

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for BAX. My reverse DCF (cost of equity 10.5%, terminal 3%, start FCF $0.55B) implies about 9.4% a year FCF growth versus my 8% base, so the price asks for more than the base case.

BAX.scenario_basis: Start underlying adjusted EPS $1.94 (guidance midpoint $2.05 less $0.11 tariff refund); EPS CAGR -6%/+8%/+16% to 2029; exit P/E 8x/11x/13x; dividend $0.04 a year; price $23.37.
kill_criteria: Organic sales growth below 1% in either of the next two quarterly reports (ex tariff effects).

Consolidated net debt / adjusted EBITDA above 4.2x (Baxter consolidated, 10-Q balance sheet and non-GAAP reconciliation), or a downgrade of senior unsecured debt to below investment grade by S&P or Moody's.
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint cut below $1.95.
Further goodwill or trade-name impairment on Front Line Care ($1.51B) or Welch Allyn ($390M).
Trailing-twelve-month FCF (operating cash flow less capex, continuing operations) below $500M at any quarter-end, or no Novum IQ US shipment resumption by 30 Jun 2027.

CTVA.thesis_one_line: Seed-and-crop-chemicals group that split in two on 1 October; the old price covered both halves, so the surviving ticker must be re-checked.
key_adverse_facts: Vylor (seed) was distributed 1-for-1 to holders of record on 24 Sep 2026 (8-K 0001193125-26-401618); post-spin CTVA is the crop-protection business plus EIDP legacy liabilities; the 25 Sep close of $78.52 is cum-distribution (combined).

H1 2026 free cash flow was about -$3.5B (operating cash flow -$3,345M, capex $203M) after a $1.46B discretionary pension contribution, a $610M Bayer settlement and an FMC prepayment (10-Q 0001755672-26-000025); seasonal, but net debt reached about $2.5B at 30 Jun 2026.
Crop Protection Q2 2026 price -4%, volume -2%, North America sales -12%; segment EBITDA margin 18.5% in Q2 and 20.8% in H1.

PFAS exposure continues: North Carolina settlement of $455M over 15 years (Corteva share about $66M) with a guarantee of Chemours' share on a 29/71 basis with DuPont and a reserve capped at $135M (8-K 0001193125-26-387254); AFFF MDL about 12,000 cases; chlorpyrifos and FTC matters; current accrued litigation $468M.
FY2025 GAAP EPS $1.75 vs operating EPS $3.34; separation costs $131M in H1 2026.
data_conflicts: d4 NTM P/E 23.3x is flagged unreliable (quarter-aware 49.6x) because of seasonality; I use the guidance midpoint $3.70 (21.2x) instead.

Two filings conflict on trading mechanics: the 14 Sep 2026 release (8-K 0001193125-26-391369) announced when-issued and ex-distribution markets from 25 Sep; the 24 Sep 2026 release (8-K 0001193125-26-401618) says no when-issued or ex-distribution trading before distribution. I rely on the later one.

The Form 10 presents Vylor as continuing operations of Corteva, Inc. and New Corteva as discontinued operations (regulatory presentation), the reverse of the economics; standalone crop-protection financials not verified.
CTVA.next_earnings_date_basis: estimate from prior-year pattern (4 Nov 2025); not announced in filings opened
CTVA.confidence_in_thesis: low for the post-spin ticker (standalone capital structure and legacy-liability split unverified); medium for the combined business, which has raised guidance repeatedly

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CTVA. On the combined company, reverse DCF (cost of equity 8.5%, terminal 3%, normalised FCF $2.7B) implies about 3.5% a year growth versus my 7% base, but the 25 Sep price does not map to the post-spin ticker, so I hold at WATCH.

CTVA.scenario_basis: Combined company (CTVA plus VYLR); start FY2026 operating EPS $3.70 (guidance midpoint); EPS CAGR 2%/8%/11% to 2029; exit P/E 16x/20x/24x; dividends $0.72 a year assumed on the combined holding; price $78.52.
kill_criteria: Crop-protection segment operating EBITDA margin below 15% (H1 26: 20.8%) in any full-year or trailing-four-quarter period reported after the separation.
Consolidated net debt / TTM Op. EBITDA of the post-spin Corteva (crop protection) above 2.5x at any quarter-end (Corteva, Inc. consolidated balance sheet).
Full-year Op. EPS guidance cut below the $3.60 low end of the 30 Jul 2026 range, or 2027 guidance implying less than 5% Op. EBITDA growth.
Accrued litigation (current, "accrued litigation" in the contingencies note; $468M at 30 Jun 2026) rising above $1.0B, or any adverse AFFF/PFAS ruling that exceeds the January 2021 MOU cost-sharing.
Crop-protection price decline worse than -4% year on year for two consecutive quarters.

IBM.thesis_one_line: Mainframe and Red Hat software giant generating about $15B a year of free cash, priced for little growth after a weak June quarter.
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 revenue +1% with Infrastructure -7% (IBM Z -42%) and Transaction Processing -8%; CEO letter of 14 Jul 2026 (8-K 0000051143-26-000070) says the team faltered.
Full-year constant-currency revenue growth guidance cut from more than 5 percent to four-to-five percent (8-K 0000051143-26-000077); H2 needs +3% to +5% against a tough Q4 comparison.
Acquisition-led growth: Confluent closed 17 Mar 2026 for $11.5B cash; goodwill $74.6B is 49% of total assets; consolidated debt $62.0B including $13.0B IBM Financing.
Operating EPS excludes acquisition amortisation; FY2025 GAAP net income of $10.6B included tax benefits; SBC $1.7B (2.5% of revenue).
An SVP sold 25,000 shares on 26 Aug 2026 (Form 4 0002005007-26-000005); IRS disputes for 2013-2018 tax years.
data_conflicts: IBM reports FY2025 FCF of $14.7B (excludes financing receivables); the Yahoo-based d4 freeCashflow is about $12.0B. Reverse DCF shown on both bases.
d4 enterprise value $271B and total debt $65.3B differ from filing debt of $62.0B at 30 Jun 2026 (aggregator timing and lease treatment).
b1 leverage 0.41 includes IBM Financing debt backed by client receivables; ex-Financing net debt is about $40.8B.
IBM.next_earnings_date_basis: estimate from prior pattern (22 Oct 2025, 22 Jul 2026); not announced in filings opened
IBM.confidence_in_thesis: medium: cash generation is well evidenced and cheap, but the July miss and acquisition-heavy growth keep it at half weight until the H2 recovery is shown

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for IBM. Reverse DCF (cost of equity 8.5-9.5%, terminal 2.5-3%) implies about -1% to 3% a year FCF growth (2% to 5% on the lower aggregator FCF) versus my 5% base.

IBM.scenario_basis: Start FY2026 consensus operating EPS $12.31; EPS CAGR 1%/6.5%/9.5% to 2029; exit P/E 13x/17x/20x; dividend $6.80 a year; price $225.51; no re-rating assumed in base.
kill_criteria: Full-year 2026 constant-currency revenue growth guidance cut below 4% (current: four-to-five percent).
Software segment revenue growth (constant currency, including acquisitions) below 3% in either Q3 or Q4 2026.
Free cash flow growth guidance of "about $1 billion" lowered, or FY2026 FCF (IBM definition) below $14.7B.
Consolidated debt excluding IBM Financing above $52B at any quarter-end without a matching rise in FCF guidance, or a downgrade to an A- equivalent or lower senior rating.
IBM Z plus Transaction Processing combined revenue still down more than 20% year on year in Q4 2026 (the first quarter against the z17 launch comparison is already past).
